Read a vector layer, stopping on a truncated shapefile

Source: R/shapefile.R
read_vector.Rd

terra::vect() with the check that read_vector_aoi() and prep_vector() apply, for code that reads a layer itself. A shapefile whose attribute table (.dbf) holds fewer records than its .shx indexes shapes is an error. GDAL would stop at the first shape without a record and return the shapes before it with only a warning; a .dbf cut at the 2 GiB dBASE size limit is in this state. Where the .shx and .dbf cannot be found beside the .shp (an archive read through /vsizip/, say), GDAL's warning that it could not read a record is made an error instead.

read_vector(src, ...)

Arguments

src

A file path or data source readable by terra::vect().

...

Passed to terra::vect(), e.g. layer, query or filter.

Value

A SpatVector.

See also

read_vector_aoi() to read only the features in an area of interest.

Examples

read_vector(system.file("ex/lux.shp", package = "terra"))
#> class       : SpatVector
#> geometry    : polygons
#> dimensions  : 12, 6  (geometries, attributes)
#> extent      : 5.74414, 6.528252, 49.44781, 50.18162  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> source      : lux.shp
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> names       :  ID_1   NAME_1  ID_2   NAME_2  AREA   POP
#> type        : <num>    <chr> <num>    <chr> <num> <num>
#> values      :     1 Diekirch     1 Clervaux   312 18081
#>                   1 Diekirch     2 Diekirch   218 32543
#>                   1 Diekirch     3  Redange   259 18664
#>               ...
